Each one appears somewhere on the site for a reason, and each is listed here with its name, its sound where it has one, and its Gardiner code — the standard catalogue Egyptologists use. About EgyBI — Who Built It, and Why: An account, only if you create one

Travellers’ notes, only if you use them — if you write a note: its text, the places and month you tag, and when you wrote it. If you mark a note helpful or report one: which note, when, and the reason you picked from the list. A note shows your display name and nothing else about you; your email address is never shown. A new account’s default display name is random, not taken from anything about you. To stop abuse, each note, mark or report also leaves a short-lived counter tied to your account and a scrambled form of your network address; these are deleted once they are a day old. A log records when the editor publishes, hides or deletes a note, and when an author deletes their own. Notes from new accounts are read by the editor before they appear, and a note that readers on more than one connection report is hidden until it is checked.

About EgyBI — Who Built It, and Why: The convention used to write foreign names: each sound of the name is matched to the uniliteral sign with the nearest value, with the usual stand-ins for vowels — the vulture for a, the reed for e and i, the quail chick for o and u. L is written with the mouth sign, as Ptolemaic scribes wrote Cleopatra’s name.
عن EgyBI — من بناه، ولماذا: العُرف المتّبع في كتابة الأسماء الأجنبية: يُطابَق كل صوت في الاسم مع العلامة الأحادية الأقرب قيمةً، مع البدائل المعتادة لحروف العلة — النسر لـa، والبوصة لـe وi، وفرخ السمّان لـo وu. ويُكتب L بعلامة الفم، كما كتب الكتبة البطالمة اسم كليوباترا.

About EgyBI — Who Built It, and Why: It is not how an Egyptian scribe would have written your name. The script recorded consonants and added signs for meaning (determinatives) that a sound-by-sound spelling leaves out; nobody in antiquity wrote vowels this way. Two tools can honestly give different spellings for the same name.
عن EgyBI — من بناه، ولماذا: ليس هو الطريقة التي كان سيكتب بها كاتب مصري اسمك. فالخط كان يدوّن الحروف الساكنة ويضيف علامات للمعنى (مخصّصات) تُسقطها الكتابة صوتًا صوتًا؛ ولم يكتب أحد في العصور القديمة حروف العلة بهذه الطريقة. ويمكن لأداتين أن تعطيا بصدق كتابتين مختلفتين للاسم نفسه.
